instruction: Buy me a cooling fan on amazon within $20 (excluding tax) and have it delivered to my home address.
notes: Fixed the name clash: the predicate formerly named home-address (same as the address object) is now is-home. Single-app (amazon) purchase task. The cooling fan is one abstract product object whose type and price bound are static init facts; amazon.search_products (query/product_type "cooling fan", max_price 20) discovers its id. Home address id comes from amazon.show_addresses (name == "Home") and a payment card id from amazon.show_payment_cards. The cart is cleared first (cart-empty) so the placed order contains exactly one item with default quantity 1, matching the evaluation (one new Order with a single OrderItem of quantity 1, product_type "cooling fan", price <= 20, delivered to the Home address, no address updates/deletions). supervisor.complete_task takes no answer; its task-record parameters (?p ?a) are not API arguments and only enforce the goal condition before completion. Every other action requires (not (task-completed)), so complete_task is necessarily last.
